title: Which providers can issue electronic attestations of attributes (EAA) for EUDI Wallets?
summary: Who can issue attestations to EUDI Wallets under eIDAS 2.0, how qualified and non-qualified attestations differ, and which providers issue them today.
body_markdown:
*Who can issue attestations to the EU Digital Identity Wallet under eIDAS 2.0, how qualified and non-qualified attestations differ, and which providers issue them today.*


Electronic attestations of attributes (EAA) for the[EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet)](https://authologic.com/blog/eudi-eidas-20-glossary-pt1#what-is-the-eudi-wallet) can be issued by trust service providers (both qualified and non-qualified) or by or on behalf of public sector bodies responsible for an authentic source. Authologic, a registered non-qualified trust service provider that runs its own EUDI Wallet infrastructure, issues EAA today; examples of providers that have announced qualified attestations (QEAA) are listed below.


*Written by dr Olga Mędraś (Head of Legal) and Florentyna Frend (Head of Product), Authologic.*
